name: web-stylebook-mcp

tools.name: recommend_design_direction
tools.description: Given product context, return scored style candidates with reason codes, rejected styles with reasons, secondary pairings, assumptions and confidence. Evidence-provider: the host model makes the final pick. Call before writing UI. The "tone" field (named "tone", not "tones") is an ARRAY of zero or more of: calm, technical, trustworthy, premium, editorial, playful, bold, experimental. Each candidate.score already includes adjustments (soft penalties, repeated-use load, closeness to avoided styles) that are not itemized in scoreBreakdown. The "ranking" field says why candidates[0] outranks the next style, or reports a tie; list the most important tone first because tone order is weighted. Each candidate.structure gives the page structure the direction implies: a layout archetype (hero composition, grid, section order, density, type-scale use), 2-3 signature moves with their purpose, and the generic and style-specific patterns audit_page_structure will flag; read structure.resourceUri for move build steps and ban criteria. The top-level mustHaves lists the elements the resolved product type requires (for example price, variant choice, add to cart, and delivery details on a commerce product page) with the zone each must sit in; a style restyles them but never removes them, they come before the archetype's limits on the opening, and each candidate.structure.mustHaves names the signature moves that can present them. Pass the same productType to audit_page_structure to find the ones a built page is missing.

tools.name: compare_design_directions
tools.description: Compare 2-4 directions across product fit, repeated-use suitability, density, trust, distinctiveness, accessibility risk, motion and maintenance. Returns each direction's favorable conditions and likely failure mode — never a single winner.

tools.name: search_design_references
tools.description: Search the bundled, attributed real-world design reference library. Query text is matched deterministically against titles, ids, categories, tags, and localized analysis. category is an exact filter; every supplied tag must match case-insensitively. Returns concise localized observations and resource links, never screenshots or brand assets.

tools.name: get_design_reference
tools.description: Return one complete localized design reference with observed palette, layout, interaction, motion, normalized tokens, source revision, CC BY attribution, adaptation notice, and original-site rights notice. Use it as research evidence; do not copy or redistribute excluded screenshots, brand assets, copy, typefaces, or visual identity.

tools.name: get_design_improvement_plan
tools.description: Default entry point for an existing-UI improvement request. Returns selected source-backed design foundations plus an executable host workflow: capture before, decide using conditional remedies and counterexamples, edit real source, verify matched after states, and report. Include context with the user task and observed target conditions; use workflow.planHash with validate_design_improvement_result to finish. Omitting context permits knowledge discovery, not completion. Select by foundationIds, concerns, surface or category (AND across dimensions, OR within concerns); bounded to 12 entries with omitted matches listed. The host AI performs edits and captures; this offline read-only MCP cannot edit files or certify visual quality. Preserve behavior and product identity; do not require a new style or stop at a review unless the user requested review only.

context.description: Observed task and target matrix for implementation and matched before/after verification; required before completion validation

dataKey.description: Same input dataset/fixture and clock, not a claim about current production data

scrollAnchor.description: Semantic location, e.g. first project or final response; pixel offsets may differ after layout changes

tools.name: validate_design_improvement_result
tools.description: Finish the existing-UI improvement workflow. Supply the exact get_design_improvement_plan query and its workflow.planHash, immutable before/fresh after captures under the planned conditions, source identities, changes with real file/diff references, observed visual/behavior/preservation/accessibility checks, per-target outcomes and limitations. Returns completion.status complete/needs-work/no-change, normalized unsupported claims, nextActions and a localized reportMarkdown with paired artifact links. Proposals, missing implementation evidence, mismatched captures, skipped targets, unsupported PASS and regressions cannot complete. Static preservation alone is insufficient. This offline tool validates host-supplied coverage and consistency only: it does not read artifacts or judge pixels, interactions, aesthetics or usability independently. Complete means the submitted evidence contract is satisfied, not independently certified improvement. Follow nextActions instead of stopping at findings.

context.description: Observed task and target matrix for implementation and matched before/after verification; required before completion validation

dataKey.description: Same input dataset/fixture and clock, not a claim about current production data

scrollAnchor.description: Semantic location, e.g. first project or final response; pixel offsets may differ after layout changes

structureRef.description: Rendered HTML or native semantic/UI hierarchy inventory

sourceRef.description: Source/build identity; distinguish the immutable baseline from the edited source

dataKey.description: Same input dataset/fixture and clock, not a claim about current production data

scrollAnchor.description: Semantic location, e.g. first project or final response; pixel offsets may differ after layout changes

steps.description: Observed interaction/accessibility procedure, not a proposed test

tools.name: get_design_principle_plan
tools.description: Select a small set of practical visual-design principles for intent and iteration, semantic hierarchy, adaptive layout and density, typography and localization, tokens and themes, accessible interaction, and complete states and recovery. Filter by design concerns, surface, phase, or explicit ids. Returns placement guidance, application steps, verification checks, cautions, related principles, and deterministic relevance scores.

matchMode.description: ranked-union scores any matched selector dimension; all-selectors requires every supplied dimension and may return no matches

tools.name: get_ux_principle_plan
tools.description: Select a small, evidence-labeled set of UX principles for a target outcome, surface, design phase, or explicit principle ids. Returns design questions, application steps, verification checks, cautions, references, and relevance scores. Treat the result as decision prompts rather than universal laws.

matchMode.description: ranked-union scores any matched selector dimension; all-selectors requires every supplied dimension and may return no matches

tools.name: get_design_audit_plan
tools.description: Return a localized, surface-aware audit checklist with stable check ids, severity, applicability, required evidence, remediation, verdict definitions, user-facing content checks, selected principle checks, and UI-state coverage. The host should confirm audit coverage and change depth with the user before choosing includeGroups. Include the opt-in "structure" group (with styleId) to add automated checks for banned generic and style-specific page patterns, answered by audit_page_structure; add productType to that group for one check per product must-have. This tool does not inspect a project: the host must collect actual rendered/code/interaction evidence, and missing evidence is NOT_VERIFIED rather than PASS.

productType.description: with the "structure" group, adds one check per must-have of this product type

revisionPreservation.description: true returns a plan of only the redesign-kept checks that compare_page_revisions answers; includeGroups may then hold only "structure" and "behavior"

tools.name: audit_page_structure
tools.description: Deterministically inspect submitted page markup (offline; the server never reads files) for the generic SaaS template (centered hero over a gradient blob, all-text centered stack, stock-photo hero, logo strip, "trusted by" band, icon feature cards, testimonial carousel, generic closing CTA banner, and the page skeleton they form) and, with styleId, for that style's own banned treatments. With productType, it also reports which of that product type's must-haves (the same list recommend_design_direction returns) the page is missing or keeps off the first screen. Pass the rendered HTML (for example document.documentElement.outerHTML) and the page's CSS text; Tailwind utility classes are understood without the stylesheet. Each finding names the location, the observed values, and what to replace it with from the chosen style's signature moves and archetype. Also returns evidence and results shaped for validate_design_audit_result with the "structure" audit group. Declared-style heuristics, not a browser: a clean result is not a design pass. Limits: html 1500000 characters, 20 stylesheets, 3000000 CSS characters in total.

productType.description: the product type passed to recommend_design_direction; adds its must-have checks

tools.name: compare_page_revisions
tools.description: Compare the original page (before) with its redesign (after), offline and deterministically, and list what the redesign kept and what it dropped: links (normalized href), form fields per form with their labels, the radio, checkbox, and select option values each field offers, the buttons each form owns, form actions and inline handlers, test hooks (data-testid, data-test, data-cy), the scriptSelectors your scripts query, h1-h3 headings, images and figures, main/nav/footer landmarks, the visible word count (Korean, Chinese, and Japanese by character), and, with productType, the must-haves audit_page_structure finds. A lost link, field, handler, script hook, or must-have, or a form left without any submit button, is FIX_NOW (major), a lost test hook FIX_NOW (minor), and lost headings, figures, landmarks, options, or other form buttons, reworded headings, links, options, or buttons, and a redesign that keeps under 60% of more than 80 words are RISK. Put intended removals in acknowledged (kind option or control for options and form buttons) with a reason of at least 12 characters. Keep the original's rendered HTML and CSS before redesigning. Returns redesign-kept-<inventory> evidence and results that validate_design_audit_result accepts with a get_design_audit_plan query of revisionPreservation: true. Static markup, not a browser. Limits per page: html 1500000 characters, 20 stylesheets, 3000000 CSS characters in total.

productType.description: compares this product type's must-haves on both pages

tools.name: validate_design_audit_result
tools.description: Regenerate the requested audit plan, then deterministically validate target coverage, evidence references, required evidence types, verdict applicability, and contradictions between verdicts and evidence outcomes. This tool does not inspect artifacts or judge visual quality. It normalizes unsupported PASS/FIX_NOW/RISK claims to NOT_VERIFIED, preserves honest NOT_VERIFIED results, and returns stable plan/evidence/result hashes for comparable rechecks. A check that names a viewport counts only on a target in that range (mobile-renders-cleanly ≤390px, desktop-composition-holds ≥1280px; answer NOT_APPLICABLE on other targets), and no-horizontal-scroll is verified across its range only with narrow (≤390px), medium (391–1439px), and wide (≥1440px) targets. Checks about the result of an action (keyboard focus, reduced motion, form errors, navigation) need after-phase interaction evidence with a passed or failed outcome. Static and before-phase evidence must match its target route; input, after, and recovery evidence may record the route an interaction led to. NOT_APPLICABLE that cites passed, failed, or indeterminate evidence is NOT_VERIFIED; record a correction or re-run as new evidence that supersedes the old item with a reason. coverage.state is full only when every slot was reported and the plan's surfaces, required states, and viewport ranges were verified or listed in scopeExclusions with a reason; coverage.reportingState covers the submitted slots alone.

productType.description: with the "structure" group, adds one check per must-have of this product type

revisionPreservation.description: true returns a plan of only the redesign-kept checks that compare_page_revisions answers; includeGroups may then hold only "structure" and "behavior"

supersedes.description: replaces an earlier evidence item of the same target and type (a re-run after a fix, or a corrected false positive); the earlier item stays in the bundle but its outcome no longer counts. The reason needs at least 12 characters

scopeExclusions.description: justified gaps in the planned scope: {surface} for a whole planned surface, {surface, stateId} for one required state, or {checkId} for the viewport range of mobile-renders-cleanly, desktop-composition-holds, or no-horizontal-scroll; each needs a reason of at least 12 characters

tools.name: get_ui_state_plan
tools.description: For a surface (data-table, form, checkout, chat, developer-console), return required / recommended / domain-specific states with triggers, must-show, must-not, accessibility and motion guidance, plus an implementation order. Covers the non-happy-path.

surfaceId.description: surface id — one of: data-table | form | checkout | chat | developer-console

styleId.description: optional catalog style id (see webstylebook://styles) to tailor state guidance

tools.name: compose_design_tokens
tools.description: Compile role-based design tokens in json / css-variables / tailwind / typescript, or as a DESIGN.md file (format "design-md", google-labs-code/design.md version alpha) that other agents and tools read: YAML tokens in the front matter or interleaved per section (designMd.tokenPlacement), localized prose, the style's Do's and Don'ts, and its page structure plus designMd.productType must-haves. The server returns the file text in content and never writes a file; values DESIGN.md has no key for (a second color mode, status colors, motion) are listed in lossy. Calls without contract keep that token shape. Their shadows follow the pinned visual contract, and editorial or monospace-led styles use authored font families; other fields remain family-derived starting points. For the full authored style and web-editor values, pass contract.schema from manifest.visualContract.contractSchema; optionally pin the manifest visualContract.contentHash and style visualContract.revision. Contract mode defaults to the authored native color mode, preserves explicit overrides, and rejects unsupported modes or a legacy secondaryStyleId overlay. Apply colors, typography, spacing, and fonts selected from another style as explicit overrides. Repairs are proposed separately; only acceptedRepairs are applied. locale controls content typography adaptation. No browser font availability or rendered appearance is claimed as verified.

accentOverride.description: 3, 6 or 8 hex digits; a missing # is added and an 8-digit alpha is kept. Without contract, a translucent accent is contrast-checked as painted on the returned canvas; any other backdrop needs a rendered review.

productType.description: adds this product type's must-haves to the Layout section

instructions: For an existing UI improvement request, default to implementation, verification and a before/after report. Use get_design_improvement_plan first, with context containing the actual user task and observed target conditions; its workflow is the default execution contract. Preserve an immutable before capture, decide with conditional design foundations and counterexamples, edit the real source using host tools, render matched after states and test affected behavior, accessibility and preservation. Call validate_design_improvement_result with the exact plan query, workflow.planHash and actual implementation/capture/check evidence. Follow nextActions for needs-work; proposals, missing evidence, mismatched conditions and regressions cannot complete an improvement. Report actual before/after artifacts, changes and reasons, verification, tradeoffs and unverified work. complete is submitted evidence coverage, not independent quality certification; no-change is never an improvement claim. A review or explanation alone is not completion unless the human explicitly requested review only. Honor explicit read-only or narrower scope. Infer a bounded scope from the task and inspect available source before asking; ask only for missing information that materially blocks execution, never for routine reapproval. Commit, push, release and deployment remain separate authorizations. Keep working behavior and product identity, and do not require a new catalog style or new-direction approval for existing-UI fixes. Record baseline strengths and compare gains against losses in grouping, visible information, continuity and reading comfort. Keep the original when benefits are unsupported; user feedback that identifies a regression reopens prior improvement claims and requires correcting the report. Familiar visual patterns are investigation cues, not automatic defects or proof of AI authorship. Source-supported concepts and authored remedies remain distinct. The host performs edits and captures; this offline MCP cannot access the project. These existing-UI instructions take precedence over the new-direction workflow below. Use Web Stylebook before implementing or redesigning UI. Explicit audit-only requests remain read-only and use get_design_audit_plan and validate_design_audit_result. For a genuinely new visual direction, start with recommend_design_direction using product context, then read webstylebook://styles/{id}. Use search_design_references to find a small set of relevant real-world examples and get_design_reference for only the selected entries; treat their observations and tokens as attributed research evidence, not permission to copy or redistribute screenshots, brand assets, copy, typefaces, or visual identity. Then call get_design_principle_plan for the layout concerns/surface/phase, call get_ux_principle_plan for the task outcomes/surface/phase, call get_ui_state_plan for each surface, and compose_design_tokens for tokens. Prefer the pinned visual contract path: pass contract.schema from manifest.visualContract.contractSchema and optionally its contentHash plus the selected style revision; omit colorMode for the authored native mode and carry the website editor overrides. Keep the complete visualContract companion when delivering CSS or a theme. Calls without contract keep the legacy token shape: shadows follow the pinned visual contract, and editorial or monospace-led styles use authored font families. Other fields remain family-derived starting points. After implementation call get_design_audit_plan and inspect the actual rendered/code/interaction evidence for every included check; missing evidence is NOT_VERIFIED, never PASS. Submit the plan query, target matrix, evidence references, and one result per check/target to validate_design_audit_result before claiming completion; its valid field describes contract validity, not visual quality. A direction changes structure, not just tokens: build from candidate.structure (layout archetype and signature moves), then run audit_page_structure on the built page’s HTML and CSS with the chosen styleId, replace every finding with the move it names, and include the "structure" audit group when validating. Style never removes a product must-have: place every entry of the recommendation’s mustHaves in its zone (a first-screen item goes in the hero, whatever the archetype’s opening limits say), and pass the same productType to audit_page_structure, which lists the ones that are missing or off the first screen. When content is in scope, lack of internal jargon is not enough: test whether material claims, conclusions, and recommendations match their support and expressed certainty; whether prominent copy conveys concrete, context-specific information; and whether visual prominence matches information value, task relevance, and support. Do not invent evidence, facts, or next steps while rewriting. Use design principles as practical placement and visual-review guidance rather than a fixed recipe. Treat UX principles as evidence-labeled decision prompts, not universal laws; accessibility, safety, informed consent, and truthful feedback take priority. The following composition guidance is only for a requested new visual direction, not the existing-UI improvement workflow. Treat results as evidence, not code; do not blindly choose candidates[0]. The chosen style is a starting tone, not a layout mold: compose the components the brief needs and adapt the style to fit (override fonts/grid where it calls for it), not a generic page in that style. Compose the opening from the product’s single most important object/action/feeling, not the SaaS template. Two columns (copy beside a visual) are fine, but the visual must be a bespoke demonstration of THIS product’s core mechanic — NOT generic furniture (a stock photo, an abstract blob, generic app chrome, or a card you could paste onto another product); a decorative seam bridging the columns does not launder a generic visual. Avoid the all-text centered-stack and giant-word defaults too, and cap opening prose at a headline + one short line + one action (the product’s must-haves, such as price, options, and delivery details on a product page, are not prose and stay). Don’t default to the AI headline cadence either — an evocative noun-phrase fragment with one word italicized in the accent color, repeated on every product; the headline must be specific to THIS product (paste-test: it couldn’t sit on a competitor by swapping a noun) and vary its form and emphasis each time. For open-ended new-direction work, first ask a short intake (available image/brand assets or whether to source license-free sample imagery, and anything to emphasize), then present 2-3 candidate directions that differ in opening STRUCTURE (not just color/tone) and wait for user approval before final component/system implementation; once a direction is approved, confirm scope and open details (deliverable, stack, real content/data, target devices) before building. This server is deterministic, read-only, offline, and does not access the project filesystem.
